text.p: (All figures in millions of French francs)

NOTE - Hermes gave its sales results in a statement. It said sales rose 9.3 percent in 1996. At constant currency rates, they would have been up 11.3 percent, but the Japanese yen's weakness had a negative impact.
Sales grew three percent in France, nine percent in the United States, 25 percent at constant exchange rates in Japan, 10 percent in Europe and 11 percent in the Asia-Pacific region.

Perfume sales rose 15 percent, helped by the launch overseas of "24, Faubourg." Sales of its silk products slipped one percent due mostly to weakness in the first half. Ready- to-wear sales rose 23 percent at constant currency rates, leather goods sales rose 17 percent, watch sales rose 18 percent, John Lobb shoe sales rose 23 percent and sales of dining table settings rose four percent.
